title: 3D Bioprinting Phototunable Hydrogels to Study Fibroblast Activation
protocol: Weigh the reactants.
Add a stir bar to a 250 mL Schlenk flask and purge with argon.
Dissolve PEG-OH in anhydrous THF within the Schlenk flask.
Add NaH to the reaction mixture and stir at room temperature for 30 min.
Add EBrMA dropwise to the reaction vessel, protected from light.
Stir the reaction at room temperature for approximately 48 h.
Add a few drops of 1 N acetic acid to quench the reaction.
Vacuum filter the solution through a filtration aid.
Concentrate the filtrate on a rotary evaporator.
Precipitate in 4 °C diethyl ether.
Leave precipitate protected from light at 4 °C for 12-18 h.
Add a Whatman filter paper to a Buchner funnel.
Slowly pour the reaction mixture over the filter paper.
Use vacuum suction to separate the precipitate from diethyl ether.
Collect the precipitate in a dry and clean filtration flask.
Vacuum dry the product for at least 5 h or overnight at room temperature.
Dissolve the dried product in minimum volume of deionized water needed.
Transfer the dissolved product into dialysis tubing.
Dialyze against 3.5 L of deionized water for at least four days.
Change the dialysis water every 12 h.
Flash-freeze the product and lyophilize for approximately 72 h or until it is completely dry.
Dissolve the product in chloroform D (CDCl3).
Run the sample using 1H NMR with a protocol that performs 248 scans with 2.5 s relaxation time.
Calibrate CDCl3 solvent peak to 7.26 PPM.
Integrate the peak for PEG backbone protons (d3.71).
Calibrate the integration to 114.
Integrate the remaining peaks in PEGαMA 1H NMR spectrum at 300 MHz in CDCl3.
Compare the integration for the αMA alkene end group peaks to the expected value based on the PEG backbone calibration.
Transfer the bioprinter and all associated parts into a biosafety cabinet using aseptic techniques.
Assemble a 30 G 0.5" length blunt needle tip to the printing glass syringe and set aside.
Plug the power cord of the bioprinter into an outlet.
Press the red power button on the front of the bioprinter to turn it on.
Connect the USB cord between the computer and bioprinter and ensure all wire connections are established and plugged in.
Prepare cell culture medium according to manufacturer's instructions with SmBM Basal Medium and SmGM-2 SingleQuots supplements, excluding FBS.
Store prepared cell culture medium at 4 °C until use.
Aliquot 50 mL of cell culture medium and add 1% v/v of FBS.
Store the low-serum media at 4 °C until use.
Resuspend gelatin slurry powder according to manufacturer's instructions using sterile cell culture media without FBS as solvent.
Adjust the final pH of the gelatin slurry to pH 9 using 2 M KOH and/or 2 M HCl as needed with a pH meter.
Fill each well of a 24-well plate approximately half full with 1 mL of gelatin slurry using a syringe without needle.
Uniformly fill the center of the wells.
Tap the plate to help evenly distribute the microparticle slurry.
Adjust the height and volume of slurry per well as needed.
Insert a correctly sized syringe plunger into a test tube containing compacted gelatin slurry.
Insert a small guide wire alongside the test tube during plunger insertion.
Remove the guide wire when the plunger contacts the gelatin slurry.
Cut off the tip of the test tube with a razor blade to create a hole for extrusion.
Press down on the syringe plunger immediately before use.
Place the filled 24-well plate onto the center of the bioprinter stage.
Secure the 24-well plate to the platform using a rubber band.
Thaw HPAAF cells in a biosafety cabinet using aseptic techniques.
Expand the thawed HPAAFs in T-75 tissue culture-treated plastic flasks containing SmBM Basal Medium and all the SmGM-2 SingleQuots supplements according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Maintain HPAAFs at 37 °C with 5% CO2 and replenish the media every few days.
Once HPAAFs have reached ~80-90% confluency, aspirate the media from each flask.
Rinse the cells one time with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Add approximately 4 mL of prewarmed 0.05% trypsin-EDTA to each T-75 flask and tilt the flask to ensure the entire cell culture surface is covered.
Incubate the flasks for 3-5 min at 37 °C and check for cell detachment.
Once cells are floating, add at least 6 mL of Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) to each flask.
Transfer the cells into a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 x g for 5 min at room temperature to pellet the cells.
Aspirate the supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cells in 1-3 mL of media with FBS using a 1000 µL pipette, ensuring a single-cell suspension.
Transfer 10 μL of the cell suspension to a microcentrifuge tube.
Add 10 μL of Trypan Blue solution and mix well.
Use 10 μL of this mixture to count cells within a hemocytometer using an inverted light microscope.
Prepare a 20 mM tris(2-carboxyethyl) phosphine (TCEP) pH 7 solution.
Sterile filter the TCEP solution using a 0.2 µm syringe filter.
Immediately before use, add 2 M KOH and/or 2 M HCl to adjust the solution pH as needed.
Measure with a pH meter and adjust accordingly.
Prepare a 0.25 mg/mL stock solution of PEGαMA in sterile cell culture media without FBS.
Resuspend 1,4-dithiothreitol (DTT) and MMP2-degradable crosslinker in 250 mM stock solutions.
Resuspend the CGRGDS peptide in a 250 mM stock solution using 20 mM sterile TCEP.
Prepare a 15 wt% stock solution of poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) in distilled water.
Combine specified amounts of PEGαMA, DTT, MMP2-degradable crosslinker, PEO, and CGRGDS with fibroblasts in a 50 mL conical tube.
Check the pH of the combined mixture with pH strips; it should be close to 6.2.
Adjust the pH if necessary by adding small volumes of pH adjusters and track added volume for final adjustments.
Add remaining low-serum cell culture media to reach a total volume of 200 µL, adjusting for any pH adjustment volume previously added.
Mix the bioink thoroughly using a positive displacement pipette to ensure cells are in single-cell suspension.
Confirm the final precursor solution is at pH 6.2 to prevent base-catalyzed polymerization during bioprinting.

Load the bioink into the glass syringe by removing the plunger and using a separate syringe attached to transfer the bioink from the centrifuge tube to the syringe, being careful to avoid forming air bubbles within the solution.
Place the glass syringe within the print head.
Attach print head components so that everything is firmly assembled and ready for printing.
Manually adjust the position of the extrusion needle into the center of a well using directional arrows in the Pronterface software.
Position the needle within the support bath slurry with at least 1 mm below the tip of the needle.
Maneuver the needle carefully within the software to ensure it will not hit any boundaries of the well.
Position the needle tip in the center of the slurry within the well.
Hit the start button within the Pronterface to begin printing.
Wait for the print to complete to achieve constructs.
Repeat steps 6.1-6.2 until the number of desired bioprinted constructs is met.
Move to the next well and reset everything if a print fails.
Leave the well plate at room temperature and cover it in the BSC for 1 h after printing.
Place the well plate containing 3D bioprinted constructs into a 37°C sterile incubator.
Leave the constructs in the incubator for 12-18 hours to melt away the support bath slurry.
Prepare a 2.2 mM lithium phenyl-2,4,6-trimethylbenzoylphosphinate (LAP) stock solution in PBS and sterile filter using a 0.2 μm syringe filter.
Keep the LAP solution protected from light.
After 12-18 hours, change the media surrounding the bioprinted constructs.
Manually remove the media and melted gelatin support bath within the wells carefully.
Slowly remove the media while holding the plate at a 45° angle to avoid disturbing the bioprinted constructs.
Add an appropriate volume of low-serum media to each well.
For a 24-well plate, add 700 µL media per well.
Return the plate to the incubator and change the media on the samples every 3 days or as needed.
Twenty-four hours before the desired stiffening time point, remove media from the samples and replace them with low-serum media supplemented with 2.2 mM sterile LAP.
Swell 3D bioprinted constructs in PBS supplemented with 10 µM methacryloxyethyl thiocarbamoyl rhodamine B overnight for fluorescent labeling.
Stiffen the labeled structure as described and transfer into PBS for 2 days at 4 °C to remove excess rhodamine.
Image using a TRITC filter.
At the desired stiffening time point, remove half of the media from the wells to be stiffened and place the plate with the lid off under UV light.
Apply 10 mW/cm² 365 nm light for 5 min using Omnicure.
Remove the remaining media from these wells and add fresh low-serum media to each well.
Return the plate to the incubator.
Take out the plate from the incubator and perform the fibroblast activation study at the desired time point.
Remove media from each well.
Rinse constructs with sterile PBS.
Incubate constructs in a live/dead staining solution containing calcein AM (1:1000 dilution) and propidium iodide (1:1000 dilution) for 40 min at 37°C on a rocker.
Transfer constructs into sterile PBS.
Image constructs immediately using a confocal fluorescence microscope, acquiring three different 100 µm z-stack images per sample per time point.
Express fibroblast viability as the average percentage of live cells.
Prepare 3% w/v bovine serum albumin (BSA) and 0.1% v/v Tween 20 in PBS to create the immunofluorescence solution.
Remove media from sample wells at desired timepoints.
Rinse constructs with PBS.
Replace PBS with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA), incubating samples at 37°C for 30 min on a rocker.
Replace PFA with 100 mM glycine in PBS, leaving samples on a rocker at room temperature for 15 min.
Transfer samples into Tissue-Tek Cryomolds and cover them completely with OCT solution.
Allow the OCT to diffuse into the samples for 12-18 h at 4°C.
Flash-freeze the OCT-soaked samples in 2-methylbutane using liquid nitrogen.
Fill a styrofoam box or other appropriate container with liquid nitrogen.
Place a second container filled with 2-methylbutane within the liquid nitrogen, submerging it at least halfway.
Hold each cryomold containing an OCT-covered sample in liquid nitrogen cooled 2-methylbutane until visibly frozen.
Store the samples at -80 °C until ready for cryosection.
Cryosection the frozen OCT samples at -22 °C and attach 10 µm thick slices to positively charged glass microscope slides.
Prepare three microscope slides with at least 3-5 cryosections per slide for each 3D hydrogel sample.
Fix the cryosections in ice-cold acetone for 15 min.
Gently rinse the cryosections with room temperature (RT) water to remove any remaining OCT.
Let the samples dry and outline the cryosections with a hydrophobic pen.
Permeabilize the samples at RT with 0.2% v/v Triton X-100 in PBS for 10 min.
Block the sections with 5% BSA w/v in PBS for 1 h at RT.
Add the primary mouse anti-human alpha smooth muscle actin (αSMA) antibody at a 1:250 dilution to the IF solution.
Store sectioned samples with the primary antibody overnight at 4 °C.
Rinse the samples three times with IF solution.

Incubate sections in IF solution containing the secondary goat anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 555 antibody at a 1:250 dilution and two drops of ActinGreen 488 ReadyProbe per milliliter of IF solution, protected from light for 1 hour at room temperature.
Rinse the sections three times with IF solution.
Incubate them in 300 nM 4',6-diamidino-2-phylindole (DAPI) in DI water for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Conduct a final rinse of the sections three times with DI water.
Use 10 µL of a commercially available antifade reagent to coverslip the sections using standard methods.
Store mounted slides protected from light in a -80 °C freezer until needed for imaging.
Upload images into ImageJ (NIH).
Quantify the percentage of αSMA positive cells as a measurement of fibroblast activation.
Divide the total number of αSMA-positive cells by the total number of cell nuclei for each field of view.
Assess fibroblast proliferation in soft and stiffened 3D bioprinted constructs.
Measure EdU positivity to quantify cell proliferation.
Analyze representative confocal images for EdU and Hoechst dye staining.
Compare the prevalence of EdU immunofluorescence between cells in soft and stiffened constructs.
Remove cell culture media from each well twenty-four hours before a desired proliferation time point.
Replace with low-serum media supplemented with 10 µM EdU solution.
Return the samples to the incubator for overnight incubation.
Fix the samples at the desired proliferation time point using 4% PFA at 37 °C for 30 min on a rocker.
Replace the 4% PFA solution with 100 mM glycine in PBS and incubate at 37 °C for at least 15 minutes.
Add Hoechst at an appropriate concentration for 30 min.
Rinse the constructs twice with PBS.
Image all fixed and stored EdU samples using a fluorescence microscope according to suggested cell proliferation kit manufacturer settings and filters.
Acquire three different 100 µm z-stack images per sample.
Create maximum projections from each of these z-stacks.
Measure HPAAF proliferation by counting the number of EdU-positive cells within the maximum projection images.
Divide the count of EdU-positive cells by the total number of cells identified by Hoechst counterstain to calculate proliferation rate.
